text:
A: Hello! Sat sri akal, ji! Can you hear me?
B: Sat sri akal! Yes, I can hear you. Hello. How are you?
A: Good, good. Last one, yeah? Everybody else is finished, it's just me and you now. Hitesh, Peterborough.
B: Gurpreet. Hayes, West London. Nice to meet you.
A: Hayes, near airport, yeah? I spoke to Marta, she said you were very patient with the puzzle. Better than me.
B: Ha, no, no. I was slow, that's it. I don't know I got it right.
A: Slow is fine, mate. I just clicked anything. What you do for work?
B: Food factory, near Heathrow. Tray-sealing line. Part-time, three shifts.
A: Three shifts! Same as me! Chilled food, Peterborough, I'm on flow-wrap, but I do tray-sealer also sometimes. When the machine jams, they call me, you know, I know all the shortcuts.
B: Shortcuts, yeah, yeah. Everybody has shortcuts on the machine.
A: Some shortcuts the supervisor doesn't like, ha. Why part-time for you? For me it's choice, I do delivery also, moped, evenings.
B: Er, my back. Two years ago I hurt it, lifting the film rolls. Physio said do less. It's okay now. Little bit hard sometimes.
A: Ah, sorry, mate. Those rolls, they're stupid heavy. They should give machine for that. You do forklift also?
B: Yes, I have the licence. From work, they paid.
A: They paid! Lucky. I'm driving forklift sometimes, but no licence, you know, just when nobody is looking. I keep saying I'll book the course. Warehouse pays better, innit.
B: Yeah, it's better. It's not so hard, the course. Few days. You should do it.
A: Yeah, yeah. I should. My wife says same. Every year I say this year. Like Dubai, I say every year. Where you're from, Punjab?
B: Yes, near Phagwara, Jalandhar side. I came at twenty-four.
A: I came twenty-six! Gujarat, Anand district. Married, came here, boom, factory. I was doing BCom, didn't finish, you know. Sometimes I think, if I stayed...
B: Yeah. Same for many people. I did ITI, fitting. Here nobody cares, you start again.
A: Exactly! Here they see you on the line, they think you're just a line guy. They don't know what's in here. But anyway, I have ideas. Phone repair stall, maybe. I can fix any phone.
B: Sorry? Phone what?
A: Phone repair. Screens, unlocking. I worked in my cousin's shop back home, years. You have broken phone, send it to Peterborough, I fix it, special price.
B: Ha. Okay, okay. My phone is fine, thank god. You watch cricket?
A: Watch? Mate, I live cricket. IPL, Mumbai Indians. Last night, our guy, dropped catch, simple. I told uncle Abdul, I told Marta, now I'm telling you. Everyone must know.
B: Yeah, I saw it. Very easy one. I watch India mostly, World Cup, big matches. Not every IPL.
A: Not every IPL? Gurpreet ji, what are you doing with your evenings?
B: Er, I call my mum. Every evening, video call. And I look after my chillies.
A: Chillies! Abdul uncle has chillies also, on the balcony. Every Indian man in this study is growing chillies except me. I just buy them from Lincoln Road. Komal says I should grow something, I said, I'm growing the kids, that's enough.
B: Ha! That's also growing, yeah, yeah. How old are your kids?
A: Dev is twelve, Riya eight. Dev wants new phone for birthday, iPhone. I said, I fix phones, I give you good old one. He said, Papa, no, everyone will—
